chunks: From him, from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUmar, from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the urine of al-khashāshīf that gets onto my garment, then I look for it but do not find it. He said: “Wash your garment.” And that is not contradicted by what he narrated:

key_terms.الْخَشَاشِيفِ: a type of small creature mentioned in the ruling concerning urine
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine; the impure substance being asked about
key_terms.ثَوْبَكَ: your garment; the object commanded to be washed
key_terms.ثَوْبِي: my garment; the item affected by impurity
key_terms.فَأَطْلُبُهُ: then I look for it; searching for the affected spot
key_terms.فَلَا أَجِدُهُ: but I do not find it; inability to locate the impurity precisely

ai.seo_question: What should be done if impurity from urine reaches a garment but its exact place cannot be found?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling of taharah regarding impurity affecting clothing. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that the garment should be washed when affected by the urine mentioned in the report, even if the exact spot cannot be found.
